hints: Notice whether the source arrow points towards the left-hand observer or away to the right in each of A, B, C and D.
Recall that motion towards stretches nothing - it crowds wavefronts together, while motion away spreads successive wavefronts further apart in the direction of the observer.
Compare the two receding cases C at $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and D at $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ to decide which gives the larger observed wavelength and therefore the lower $f = v / \lambda_{obs}$.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry: the observer is on the left and the source is on the right. In A and B the $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ arrows point left, towards the observer. In C and D the arrows point right, away from the observer.

State the Doppler rule for a moving source and stationary observer: approaching decreases observed wavelength $\lambda_{obs}$ and increases $f_{obs}$, receding increases $\lambda_{obs}$ and decreases $f_{obs}$.
Therefore the lowest frequency must be one of the receding cases, C or D, because only recession stretches the waves reaching the left-hand observer.

For recession, faster speed means the source travels further between emissions, so $\lambda_{obs}$ is larger. D at $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ away stretches $\lambda_{obs}$ more than C at $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ away.
Since $f_{obs} = v / \lambda_{obs}$ with sound speed $v$ constant, largest $\lambda_{obs}$ gives smallest $f_{obs}$. This is option D.

options.A: Source moves at $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ towards the observer, compressing wavefronts ahead so observed wavelength decreases and frequency increases.
options.B: Source moves at $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ towards the observer, giving the greatest compression of wavefronts and so the highest observed frequency.
options.C: Source moves away from the observer at $5 \text{m s}^{-1}$, stretching the wavelength and lowering frequency, but less than the faster recession.
options.D: Source moves away from the observer fastest at $10 \text{m s}^{-1}$, giving maximum stretching of observed wavelength and so minimum observed frequency.
